newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria to sell more state-owned companies.
newsitem.headline: Algeria to sell more state-owned companies.

text.p: Algeria will offer more state-owned companies for sale soon as well as shut down some small businesses run by local authorities, the official Algerian news agency APS said on Monday.
The agency quoted the State Participations Council, a government board which controls the management of state-run companies, as refusing to name any of the firms involved.
The new privatisation move was announced a few weeks after President Liamine Zeroual deplored the fact that only 10 state companies had been sold to private capital.
Algerian managers and officials in charge of privatisation were holding a conference on Monday on how to handle the changes with World Bank experts in Algiers.

Officials see the conference as the latest round of debates on privatisation which had been delayed by fears over its impact on unemployment, which already affects more than two million of the country's five million workforce.

A World Bank expert, quoted by APS, said the best scenario for Algeria was a phased privatisation process in which the government could sell 300 enterprises among the 1,350 state-owned privatisable companies.
